title: Does Claude just remember where it left off?
text: Someone assumes an agent picking up mid-project must remember where it stopped like memory carries over. It doesn't. It rereads a file that tracks progress. Here's how that actually works. A context window has a limit.

title: The session boundary is a wipe
text: When an agent's conversation fills it, the session ends. The next session opens blank, no memory of what was done, what passed, what failed. Rereading everything burns half the new context, guessing risks getting it wrong. The fix

title: Two files hold the truth
text: To external files. feature_list.json is the source of truth, 200 entries each with an ID and a status, incomplete or passing. Git is the ledger, one commit per finished feature, so the history can't be disputed. Each session reads the file, finds the first incomplete entry, implements it, tests it, commits, and marks it passing. Watch the file

title: The file, across the boundary
text: Itself across the boundary. Session one flips features one through 50 from incomplete to passing, one commit at a time. The boundary passes. Session two opens the same file, finds item 51 as the first incomplete entry, and starts there, no replay of the first 50. This

title: Exactly this far
text: Covers the checkpoint and resume mechanism only, the file, the Git ledger, the boundary, and the first incomplete lookup. It doesn't cover how the 200 item list gets written in the first place, that's a separate step, or what exactly makes a feature count as passing. A context

title: Carry-out
text: Window is a workspace, not memory. When it fills, the session ends, and what carries over is whatever got written to a file and a Git commit, not anything the agent remembers.

title: Your turn
text: Your turn, here's the prompt, read it with me. Ask Claude externalize my agent's progress to a checkpoint file plus Git commits, so a brand new session can resume exactly where the last one stopped, then prove it by starting a fresh session and watching it pick up correctly. Liam in for Bear. Persisting progress
